(gstack)\n- ai-check: Use when someone asks \"does this sound AI?\", \"check if this is AI-written\", \"what gives this away as AI\", \"run ai-check on this\", or \"score this text\". Also use when reviewing a draft for AI tells before publishing, or when a piece of text reads as suspiciously polished, generic, or pattern-y and the user wants a forensic breakdown of why.\n- browse: Fast headless browser for QA testing and site dogfooding. (gstack)\n- careful: Safety guardrails for destructive commands. (gstack)\n- check-citations: Verify academic citations against CrossRef, Semantic Scholar, and OpenAlex. Detects AI-hallucinated references, chimeric citations, and suspicious patterns.\n- computer-use: Drives the GUI of a visible local app window through `orca computer`: accessibility tree, clicks, typing, menus, dialogs, and screenshots in native apps and external browser windows (Chrome, Edge, Safari) or webviews. Prefer a programmatic path (shell, filesystem, git, HTTP, existing CLIs) whenever it can complete the task. Use only when a visible window needs GUI control those cannot reach. Do not use for Orca's embedded browser (`orca-cli`).\n- convert-documents-to-markdown: Convert Word (.doc, .docx), PowerPoint (.ppt, .pptx), Excel (.xls, .xlsx), OpenDocument (.odt, .ods, .odp), RTF, EPUB, CSV, and PDF files to GitHub-Flavored Markdown. Use when a task needs the contents of an office document, spreadsheet, presentation, ebook, or PDF you cannot read directly.\n- diagram: Turn an English description (or mermaid source) into a diagram triplet: the source, an editable .excalidraw file you can open on excalidraw.com, and rendered SVG + PNG. (gstack)\n- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.\n- editor-diff: Diff two versions of the same document (old and new), identifying specific\neditorial changes with location/character metadata. Characterizes the editorial\njudgement for each change, clusters diffs into a taxonomy of editorial types,\nand generates a comprehensive editor-diff-audit.md alongside the new file.\nLaTeX-aware: distinguishes content edits from formatting/macro changes.\nRejects unrelated documents (>50% changed) or identical files.\n- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.\n- gstack: Router for the gstack skill suite. (gstack)\n- gstack-upgrade: Upgrade gstack to the latest version.\n- last30days: Research a topic from the last 30 days on Reddit + X + Web, become an expert, and write copy-paste-ready prompts for the user's target tool.\n- latex-fmt: Reformat LaTeX papers for target journals and conferences. Handles document class changes, margin/page adjustments, citation style conversion, figure/table reformatting, and compliance checking against venue-specific requirements.\n- latex-polish: Polish academic writing in LaTeX files. Enhances clarity, fixes grammar, improves academic style, and eliminates Chinglish patterns. Operates on text content while preserving LaTeX commands, math, citations, and references.\n- latex-rhythm-refiner: Post-process LaTeX project prose to improve readability through varied sentence and paragraph lengths. Removes filler phrases and unnecessary transitions while preserving all citations and semantic meaning. Use after drafting is complete, when sections read as monotonous or blocky.\n- make-pdf: Turn any markdown file into a publication-quality PDF. (gstack)\n- orchestration-tiers: Reference for the Fable 5.1 orchestrator's delegation tiers (scout-haiku, clerk-haiku, worker-sonnet, worker-opus, fork), the inline-vs-dispatch rule, parallel caps and worktree isolation. Load before dispatching subagents or when unsure which tier a subtask belongs to.\n- paper-read: Read, analyze, and extract knowledge from academic papers. Handles PDFs and arXiv links. Produces structured summaries, identifies core contributions, evaluates methodology, and enables cross-paper comparison.\n- proofreading: Proofread an academic paper against a structured checklist covering abbreviations, math notation, introduction structure, grammar and style, figures and tables, and statistical relevance. Two modes — report (full written report) and interactive (fix issues step by step together with the user).\n- spec: Turn vague intent into a precise, executable spec in five phases. (gstack)\n- unslop: Humanize LLM output so it reads like a careful human wrote it. Subtracts AI-isms (sycophancy, tricolons, em-dash overuse, \"delve\"/\"tapestry\"/\"testament\", hedging stacks, tidy five-paragraph shapes), engineers burstiness and calibrated uncertainty, and preserves technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: subtle, balanced (default), full, voice-match, anti-detector. Use when user says \"humanize this\", \"make this sound human\", \"de-slop this\", \"rewrite without AI tone\", \"match my voice\", \"less robotic\", or invokes /unslop. Also auto-triggers when text-quality is requested.\n- wiki-editor: Wikipedia article editorial compliance checker. Reads .md or .wiki drafts,\nchecks against WP:MOS, WP:RS, WP:NPOV, WP:BLP, WP:GNG, detects AI writing\npatterns, verifies reference URLs, and outputs a ranked critique plus a\ncorrected article. Use when proofing Wikipedia drafts before submission.\n- proofread-grammar: Check English grammar, spelling, and phrasing in a LaTeX statistics paper\n- proofread-technical: Review a LaTeX statistics paper for notation, assumptions, and suspicious logical gaps\n- codex:rescue: Delegate investigation, an explicit fix request, or follow-up rescue work to the Codex rescue subagent\n- codex:setup: Check whether the local Codex CLI is ready and optionally toggle the stop-time review gate\n- superpowers:brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.\n- superpowers:diagnosing-superpowers: Use when a superpowers session went wrong and your human partner wants to know why — repeated work, ignored plans, stumbles, poor results, a skill that didn't fire, \"it took too long\", \"why is it so expensive\", \"what is it doing\" — or wants to build a bug report for the superpowers maintainers, for the current session or a past one identified by id or path, on any harness.\n- superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies\n- superpowers:executing-plans: Use when executing an implementation plan in the current session as the implementer yourself — your human partner chose inline execution, or no subagent tool is available\n- superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work\n- superpowers:receiving-code-review: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation\n- superpowers:requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements\n- superpowers:subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session\n- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes\n- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code\n- superpowers:using-git-worktrees: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback\n- superpowers:using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions\n- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always\n- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code\n- superpowers:writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment\n- codex:codex-cli-runtime: Internal helper contract for calling the codex-companion runtime from Claude Code\n- codex:codex-result-handling: Internal guidance for presenting Codex helper output back to the user\n- codex:gpt-5-4-prompting: Internal guidance for composing Codex and GPT-5.4 prompts for coding, review, diagnosis, and research tasks inside the Codex Claude Code plugin\n- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".\n- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.\n- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.\n- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.\n- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.\nTRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it \"looks like a one-liner\" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).\nSKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).\n- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.\n- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.\n- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.\n- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.\n- anthropic-skills:google-workspace: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even \"change it\" or \"add a tab\". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files.\n- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.\n- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.\n- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.\n- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.\n- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like \"the xlsx in my downloads\") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.\n</system-reminder>"}],"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/jonc/code/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter","sessionId":"b1d69112-f141-4bda-9d3c-4da043759227","version":"2.1.284","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"78530744-0fc2-42f2-86bd-0a108e51358c","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"instructions","files":[{"path":"/Users/jonc/.claude/CLAUDE.md","type":"User","content":"# CLAUDE.md — global rules\n\nThese apply to every project. For domain-specific rules, check subfolder `CLAUDE.md`\nfiles (e.g. `src/api/CLAUDE.md`) or files in `docs/`.\n\n## Package Management\n**Always use `uv` for all Python package operations.**\n\n- Do **not** use `pip`, `pip3`, `pip install`, or `python -m pip`.\n- Adding packages: `uv add <package>` (use `--dev` for development dependencies).\n- Syncing environment: `uv sync`\n- Running commands: `uv run <command>` (e.g. `uv run python script.py`)\n\n## Reading Large Files\nWhen inspecting large files (logs, datasets, OCR output, long documents):\n\n1. First run `wc -l <filename>` to check the line count.\n2. If the file exceeds **2,000 lines**, **do not** read the entire file at once.\n3. Use the Read tool with **offset** and **limit** (e.g. 500–1,000 lines at a time).\n4. Analyze chunk by chunk and synthesize gradually — this prevents context overflow.\n\n## Security\nNever hardcode credentials or secrets. Validate inputs. Follow least-privilege.\n\n## gstack\nUse the `/browse` skill from gstack for **all web browsing**. Never use\n`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools directly.\n\n## Skill routing (avoid fuzzy/overlapping invocation)\n\n**The repo's ai-profile decides the SDLC kit** (`.claude/ai-profile`, written by\n`ai-profile <name>`; `ai-profile init` = `fullstack`, the default for any new heavy\nAI-coding repo). No profile enables Superpowers: `fullstack` → mattpocock kit\n(`/grill-with-docs` → `/domain-modeling` → `/to-spec` → `/to-tickets` → wave dispatch or\n`/tdd` → `npm run gate` → `/code-review` → close tickets by hand, Status `closed (merged\n<date> as <sha>)`; no `/gate` or `/ticket-close` command exists), `library` → mattpocock `/tdd` +\n`/code-review`, `experiment` → mattpocock thin skills on demand, `writing` → none.\nSuperpowers stays installed at user scope but is off by default: `~/.claude/settings.json`\nsets `\"superpowers@claude-plugins-official\": false` under `enabledPlugins` (since\n2026-10-01), and a repo enables it only by an explicit `true` entry in its own\n`.claude/settings.json` (a deliberate per-repo decision, recorded in its ai-profile\nnote). Do not add per-repo `false` entries; they are redundant. Off by default because\nits SessionStart hook injects a \"skill before any action\" directive on\nstartup/clear/compact that competes with other re-injection hooks (run ledger,\norchestrator gate). Never mix two kits in one repo; in an\nunprofiled repo run `ai-profile init` before adopting any kit. (GSD was retired\n2026-09-13 — upstream `gsd-build/get-shit-done` is archived; its agents/commands/hooks\nare in `~/.claude/backups/gsd-retired-20260913.tgz`.)\n\n- **Planning / phases / roadmaps** → `/to-spec` → `/to-tickets` (mattpocock) in\n  fullstack/library repos, `/to-spec` or `/to-prd` in experiment repos; Superpowers\n  `brainstorming` → `writing-plans` → `executing-plans` only in a repo that enables it.\n  Never substitute one kit's planner for another's. Legacy `.planning/` dirs are inert\n  GSD artifacts, not a signal.\n- **Debugging** → `/diagnosing-bugs` (mattpocock); Superpowers `systematic-debugging`\n  only in a repo that enables it. Legacy `/diagnose` is superseded.\n- **Code review** → `/security-review` for security; `/code-review` (mattpocock)\n  for branch/spec reviews when I ask by name. Don't auto-run reviews.\n- **TDD** → `/tdd` only when I ask for test-first work.\n- **Handoff** → `/handoff` (my custom project-restart brief, written to `docs/handoffs/`\n  and imported via `@docs/handoffs/LATEST.md`) is the default; `/handoff-load` re-anchors\n  mid-session. `/claude-handoff` was retired 2026-09-15 (use `/fork` or a background agent).\n- **Skill authoring** → `/write-a-skill`; don't mix with skill-creator plugin.\n- **Web browsing** → `/browse` (see gstack rule below).\n- The skills above are slash-only by design (`disable-model-invocation: true`).\n  If a skill I expect is missing, check `skillOverrides` in `settings.json`\n  before reinstalling — entries set to \"off\" hide skills that are on disk.\n- **Exception**: `domain-modeling` (mattpocock) is agent-invocable\n  (`disable-model-invocation` removed from its `SKILL.md`) so it can be\n  chained from other skills, e.g. `/grill-with-docs`. Don't re-add the flag\n  out of habit when touching that file.\n\n## Git Workflow (solo trunk-based — applies to ALL agents and subagents)\nI am a solo developer. Default to trunk-based development:\n\n- **Commit only when I ask**, and commit on the **current branch**. Never\n  switch branches or create branches/worktrees on your own initiative.\n- **Never push unless I explicitly ask.** When I do, push only `main` (and\n  tags). Agent/task branches must NEVER be pushed to origin.\n- **Worktree/branch lifecycle**: if a task genuinely needs an isolated\n  worktree (parallel subagents), prefer the built-in `isolation: \"worktree\"`\n  mechanism. Any branch created is ephemeral: born, merged back, and deleted\n  within the same session. Before merging, rebase the branch on `main` so\n  conflicts surface in the branch, never in `main`.\n- **Merges are my gate**: show me a diff/test summary and wait for my\n  approval before merging to `main`, then delete the branch immediately.\n- **Decompose parallel work by file ownership**: subtasks should touch\n  disjoint files whenever possible so merges are trivially clean.\n- **Wave dispatch discipline** (parallel multi-agent ticket/task batches):\n  - Commit all of a batch's task/ticket definitions before creating any\n    worktree for that batch — untracked files don't propagate into a new\n    `git worktree add` checkout, so worktrees created first silently start\n    without them.\n  - Before dispatching a batch in parallel, pre-scan each subtask's likely\n    touches to shared cross-cutting files (registries, allowlists, config\n    tables no single subtask owns). If 2+ will touch the same file, fix\n    merge order upfront or split the shared edit into its own small\n    pre-batch task — don't let it surface for the first time as a merge\n    conflict.\n  - Any subtask's claim that it mirrors/wires-against an existing pattern\n    must cite the real command/check that verified the pattern actually\n    exists and is actually used in production, not just that a referenced\n    module exists.\n  - Before dispatching a batch's own integration/composition step, run a\n    bounded lookahead pass (a few minutes, not exhaustive) tracing the\n    batch's subtask claims against each other for cross-subtask assumption\n    mismatches — this is layered on top of the per-subtask check above, not\n    a replacement: two subtasks can each honestly verify their own claim in\n    isolation and still combine into a broken assumption neither could see\n    alone.\n- If a repo has an active `ai-profile` (see `.claude/ai-profile`), its\n  project CLAUDE.md rules extend these.\n\n## Large-file storage (this Mac)\nModel weights, caches, container images and VM disks live on the external 4 TB OWC\nExpress 1M2 SSD at `/RESEARCH_SSD` (a synthetic.conf link to `/System/Volumes/Data/RESEARCH_SSD`; not under `/Volumes`); the internal disk is 926 GB and fills.\nLayout: `ai_caches/{huggingface,ollama_models,lmstudio,hf_gguf,uv}`, `orbstack/data`,\n`docker_data/DockerDesktop`, `stacks/`. The exports (`HF_HOME`, `HF_DATASETS_CACHE`,\n`OLLAMA_MODELS`, `UV_CACHE_DIR`, `UV_LINK_MODE`) live in the guarded \"STORAGE & AI CACHE\"\nblock of `~/.zshenv` (moved from `~/.zshrc` 2026-09-03 so non-interactive shells get it too), set only while the volume is mounted. When configuring any tool that\ndownloads models, caches packages or builds images, point its data directory under\n`/RESEARCH_SSD/` and guard on the mount the same way; a large download landing on\nthe internal disk is a bug to fix, not a default to accept.\n\n## Model orchestration hierarchy (global, deterministic where the tooling allows)\nReference: `~/code/theailab-net-dev/dev-notes/orchestration_hierarchy_20260904.md` (v2, 2026-09-04).\n\n- **Supervisory orchestrator = the interactive session's model, required to be Fable 5.1.**\n  `~/.claude/settings.json` pins `model: claude-fable-5-1[1m]`. A global hook\n  (`~/.claude/hooks/orchestrator_gate.py`, wired on SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit) records the\n  live model id from the status line. On any other model the gate is ACTIVE: the first ordinary\n  prompt passes with a directive, every later one is held until I confirm. Headless `claude -p`\n  runs and `CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_GATE=0` bypass the hold. `orchestrator: status` prints the gate\n  state.\n- **Per-project override**: a `model` key in `<repo>/.claude/settings.local.json` or\n  `<repo>/.claude/settings.json` (local wins) is that repo's required orchestrator, ahead of the\n  global pin; env `ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED_MODEL` beats both. Claude Code reads the same key at\n  launch, so a pinned repo starts on and is gated to one model. `/model` only rewrites the global\n  default, so switching in one repo never changes another pinned repo's gate.\n- **Claude, when the injected gate line says ACTIVE or the model is unknown: do not act on the\n  prompt. Call AskUserQuestion with exactly three options, in order:** (1) Switch to Fable 5.1\n  (tell me to type `/model claude-fable-5-1` and re-send; the hook cannot switch models),\n  (2) Keep this model for the session (then run\n  `python3 ~/.claude/hooks/orchestrator_gate.py confirm --session <id>` via Bash, the id is in\n  the gate line, and carry out the prompt), (3) Stop. While held, the hook accepts `1`/`2`/`3`,\n  `keep`, `yes`, or `confirm orchestrator` as answers and hands the held prompt back on confirm.\n- **The orchestrator keeps** decomposition, synthesis, critique, integration and every decision;\n  **it delegates everything else** to the tier agents in `~/.claude/agents/`: `scout-haiku`\n  (read-only lookups), `clerk-haiku` (decided mechanical changes), `worker-sonnet` (default builder),\n  `worker-opus` (hard, bounded); `fork` only when the whole conversation is needed. Full tier\n  definitions, the dispatch brief template and the route-hint rules: `/orchestration-tiers`.\n- **Inline only what costs less than a dispatch** (one short command, a read under ~200 lines, a\n  one-line edit). Hook route hints are advice, not a hold: override with one line of reason.\n- **Parallelism**: cap 3 concurrent workers (burst 6 read-only/remote); mutating workers get\n  `isolation: \"worktree\"` + disjoint file ownership; verification in the foreground, one command\n  at a time.\n- **Report contract**: every subagent writes its findings to a named file (`reports/<agent>_<slug>.md`\n  or the scratchpad) and prints the path as its last line; I do not synthesize until every\n  expected report exists — a missing file is re-dispatched, never assumed.\n\n## Working agreements (from /insights 2026-09-14)\n- Front-load constraints (tools, files owned, models, containers = Podman, no push) in the dispatch\n  brief before any multi-agent or multi-file task; do not add them mid-flight — a violated\n  constraint is a restart, not a patch.\n- Name the verification inside the task (import test, symlink check, hook smoke test, `make gate`\n  subset) and run it before saying done; show the output.\n- Never overwrite a source document: write `<name>-v2.md` and say so.\n- Prefer a one-line free-text question to an AskUserQuestion picker for open-ended decisions;\n  pickers only for 2–4 mutually exclusive options.\n- After two failed corrections on the same issue, stop, suggest `/clear`, and re-brief.\n\n---\n\nIf a rule is broken, respond with: \"Update CLAUDE.md so this doesn't happen again.\"\n\n@RTK.md"}],"changed":true,"reason":"session_start"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"7574f8ca-370a-483b-931b-9a265218897e","timestamp":"2026-10-04T07:03:36.953Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nInstruction files were re-read when this session started; these differ from their earlier copies — each replaces its earlier copy, and the instructions preamble above still applies:\n\nContents of /Users/jonc/.claude/CLAUDE.md (user's private global instructions for all projects):\n\n# CLAUDE.md — global rules\n\nThese apply to every project. Before merging, rebase the branch on `main` so\n  conflicts surface in the branch, never in `main`.\n- **Merges are my gate**: show me a diff/test summary and wait for my\n  approval before merging to `main`, then delete the branch immediately.\n- **Decompose parallel work by file ownership**: subtasks should touch\n  disjoint files whenever possible so merges are trivially clean.\n- **Wave dispatch discipline** (parallel multi-agent ticket/task batches):\n  - Commit all of a batch's task/ticket definitions before creating any\n    worktree for that batch — untracked files don't propagate into a new\n    `git worktree add` checkout, so worktrees created first silently start\n    without them.\n  - Before dispatching a batch in parallel, pre-scan each subtask's likely\n    touches to shared cross-cutting files (registries, allowlists, config\n    tables no single subtask owns). If 2+ will touch the same file, fix\n    merge order upfront or split the shared edit into its own small\n    pre-batch task — don't let it surface for the first time as a merge\n    conflict.\n  - Any subtask's claim that it mirrors/wires-against an existing pattern\n    must cite the real command/check that verified the pattern actually\n    exists and is actually used in production, not just that a referenced\n    module exists.\n  - Before dispatching a batch's own integration/composition step, run a\n    bounded lookahead pass (a few minutes, not exhaustive) tracing the\n    batch's subtask claims against each other for cross-subtask assumption\n    mismatches — this is layered on top of the per-subtask check above, not\n    a replacement: two subtasks can each honestly verify their own claim in\n    isolation and still combine into a broken assumption neither could see\n    alone.\n- If a repo has an active `ai-profile` (see `.claude/ai-profile`), its\n  project CLAUDE.md rules extend these.\n\n## Large-file storage (this Mac)\nModel weights, caches, container images and VM disks live on the external 4 TB OWC\nExpress 1M2 SSD at `/RESEARCH_SSD` (a synthetic.conf link to `/System/Volumes/Data/RESEARCH_SSD`; not under `/Volumes`); the internal disk is 926 GB and fills.\nLayout: `ai_caches/{huggingface,ollama_models,lmstudio,hf_gguf,uv}`, `orbstack/data`,\n`docker_data/DockerDesktop`, `stacks/`. The exports (`HF_HOME`, `HF_DATASETS_CACHE`,\n`OLLAMA_MODELS`, `UV_CACHE_DIR`, `UV_LINK_MODE`) live in the guarded \"STORAGE & AI CACHE\"\nblock of `~/.zshenv` (moved from `~/.zshrc` 2026-09-03 so non-interactive shells get it too), set only while the volume is mounted. When configuring any tool that\ndownloads models, caches packages or builds images, point its data directory under\n`/RESEARCH_SSD/` and guard on the mount the same way; a large download landing on\nthe internal disk is a bug to fix, not a default to accept.\n\n## Model orchestration hierarchy (global, deterministic where the tooling allows)\nReference: `~/code/theailab-net-dev/dev-notes/orchestration_hierarchy_20260904.md` (v2, 2026-09-04).\n\n- **Supervisory orchestrator = the interactive session's model, required to be Fable 5.1.**\n  `~/.claude/settings.json` pins `model: claude-fable-5-1[1m]`. A global hook\n  (`~/.claude/hooks/orchestrator_gate.py`, wired on SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit) records the\n  live model id from the status line. On any other model the gate is ACTIVE: the first ordinary\n  prompt passes with a directive, every later one is held until I confirm. Headless `claude -p`\n  runs and `CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_GATE=0` bypass the hold. `orchestrator: status` prints the gate\n  state.\n- **Per-project override**: a `model` key in `<repo>/.claude/settings.local.json` or\n  `<repo>/.claude/settings.json` (local wins) is that repo's required orchestrator, ahead of the\n  global pin; env `ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED_MODEL` beats both. Claude Code reads the same key at\n  launch, so a pinned repo starts on and is gated to one model. `/model` only rewrites the global\n  default, so switching in one repo never changes another pinned repo's gate.\n- **Claude, when the injected gate line says ACTIVE or the model is unknown: do not act on the\n  prompt. Call AskUserQuestion with exactly three options, in order:** (1) Switch to Fable 5.1\n  (tell me to type `/model claude-fable-5-1` and re-send; the hook cannot switch models),\n  (2) Keep this model for the session (then run\n  `python3 ~/.claude/hooks/orchestrator_gate.py confirm --session <id>` via Bash, the id is in\n  the gate line, and carry out the prompt), (3) Stop. While held, the hook accepts `1`/`2`/`3`,\n  `keep`, `yes`, or `confirm orchestrator` as answers and hands the held prompt back on confirm.\n- **The orchestrator keeps** decomposition, synthesis, critique, integration and every decision;\n  **it delegates everything else** to the tier agents in `~/.claude/agents/`: `scout-haiku`\n  (read-only lookups), `clerk-haiku` (decided mechanical changes), `worker-sonnet` (default builder),\n  `worker-opus` (hard, bounded); `fork` only when the whole conversation is needed. Full tier\n  definitions, the dispatch brief template and the route-hint rules: `/orchestration-tiers`.\n- **Inline only what costs less than a dispatch** (one short command, a read under ~200 lines, a\n  one-line edit). Hook route hints are advice, not a hold: override with one line of reason.\n- **Parallelism**: cap 3 concurrent workers (burst 6 read-only/remote); mutating workers get\n  `isolation: \"worktree\"` + disjoint file ownership; verification in the foreground, one command\n  at a time.\n- **Report contract**: every subagent writes its findings to a named file (`reports/<agent>_<slug>.md`\n  or the scratchpad) and prints the path as its last line; I do not synthesize until every\n  expected report exists — a missing file is re-dispatched, never assumed.\n\n## Working agreements (from /insights 2026-09-14)\n- Front-load constraints (tools, files owned, models, containers = Podman, no push) in the dispatch\n  brief before any multi-agent or multi-file task; do not add them mid-flight — a violated\n  constraint is a restart, not a patch.\n- Name the verification inside the task (import test, symlink check, hook smoke test, `make gate`\n  subset) and run it before saying done; show the output.\n- Never overwrite a source document: write `<name>-v2.md` and say so.\n- Prefer a one-line free-text question to an AskUserQuestion picker for open-ended decisions;\n  pickers only for 2–4 mutually exclusive options.\n- After two failed corrections on the same issue, stop, suggest `/clear`, and re-brief.\n\n---\n\nIf a rule is broken, respond with: \"Update CLAUDE.md so this doesn't happen again.\"\n\n@RTK.md\n</system-reminder>"}],"renderedRole":"user","session_id":"e8e2fd01-c177-4a4e-8c7d-e75327a36451","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/jonc/code/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter","sessionId":"b1d69112-f141-4bda-9d3c-4da043759227","version":"2.1.289","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"361a0aeb-d666-4abd-8ef5-b281d76cc000","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"eb0fdf65-dae4-4273-856a-bb152fd3e61b","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012cuaDQtrLvQqeQHSMCNJ3k","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t#!/usr/bin/env python3\n2\t\"\"\"\n3\torchestrator_gate.py -- global model-orchestration hierarchy for Claude Code (stdlib only). v2.\n4\t\n5\tPolicy (durable, machine-wide; see ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md \"Model orchestration hierarchy\"):\n6\t  * The interactive session's model is the SUPERVISORY ORCHESTRATOR. It is expected to be the\n7\t    REQUIRED_MODEL resolved per project (see resolve_required()/configure_required(): env\n8\t    ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED_MODEL, then the `model` key of <cwd>/.claude/settings.local.json and\n9\t    <cwd>/.claude/settings.json, then of ~/.claude/settings.json, then the hardcoded Fable 5.1).\n10\t    Claude Code reads the same project `model` key at launch, so one key pins both the session's\n11\t    model and the gate. If a session runs on anything else, the user must confirm that choice\n12\t    before ordinary prompts are processed.\n13\t  * The orchestrator keeps decomposition, synthesis, critique and decisions and delegates\n14\t    everything else to cheaper named tiers (~/.claude/agents/): scout-haiku (read-only lookups),\n15\t    clerk-haiku (mechanical state changes: git, CLI runs, bulk edits), worker-sonnet (default\n16\t    builder), worker-opus (hard but bounded). CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL is the floor for any\n17\t    subagent dispatched without a model.\n18\t\n19\tSubcommands (first CLI argument; hook payload JSON on stdin unless noted):\n20\t  session-start   SessionStart hook: record the session, inject the policy + gate state\n21\t  prompt          UserPromptSubmit hook: see \"Gate flow\" below; also injects a routing hint for\n22\t                  prompts that match a mechanical/lookup pattern (see route_prompt), and, once per\n23\t                  10-point band from 50% up (or when the repo's task-boundary verdict flips), a\n24\t                  context handoff nudge carrying that verdict (see context_nudge / boundary_state)\n25\t  statusline      statusLine command: record model.id and context_window.used_percentage for the\n26\t                  session, then run\n27\t                  ~/.claude/hooks/statusline_inner.sh with the same stdin (fallback: minimal line)\n28\t  record          record model.id from a statusLine-shaped JSON on stdin (for per-repo status lines)\n29\t  confirm         --session <id> [--model <id>]: record the user's \"keep this model\" decision.\n30\t                  Run by Claude (via Bash) after the user picks \"Keep\" in the AskUserQuestion menu.\n31\t  route           [--hint] <prompt text...>: print the tier route_prompt() picks (manual check)\n32\t  status          print the gate state for the current/most recent sessions (human use)\n33\t  self-test       deterministic smoke scenarios in a temp state dir; exit 1 on failure\n34\t                  (the full suite is ~/.claude/hooks/tests/test_orchestrator_gate.py)\n35\t\n36\tGate flow for an interactive session on a non-required model (the v1 flow held the FIRST prompt,\n37\twhich meant Claude never got the turn it needed to show the promised AskUserQuestion menu, and the\n38\thold only accepted a prompt beginning with the literal phrase \"confirm orchestrator\" -- eight natural\n39\tanswers typed by the user on 2026-09-04 were all held; see tests/test_orchestrator_gate.py):\n40\t  1. The first ordinary prompt PASSES, with a directive that Claude must call AskUserQuestion\n41\t     (Switch / Keep / Stop) before acting, and record \"Keep\" with `confirm --session <id>`.\n42\t  2. Every later ordinary prompt is HELD (exit 2, menu on stderr) until confirmed. While held, the\n43\t     menu answers are accepted as prompts: 1/switch, 2/keep/yes/ok/confirm, 3/restart/stop/exit,\n44\t     plus \"confirm orchestrator\" anywhere in the text. The held prompt is remembered and handed\n45\t     back to Claude on confirmation, so the user does not have to re-type it.\n46\t  3. A /model switch re-arms the gate for the new model (the status line records the change).\n47\t\n48\tHow the model is known (hook payloads carry no model field; measured 2026-09-04, 2.1.26x):\n49\t  1. the per-session record written by `statusline`/`record` (fresh on every render, incl. /model)\n50\t  2. the last assistant entry's `message.model` in the session transcript (resume / later turns)\n51\t  3. otherwise UNKNOWN: never blocked; Claude is told to state its model and, if it is not the\n52\t     required one, to run the same AskUserQuestion menu and confirm with --model.\n53\t\n54\tEscapes (deliberate, explicit): CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_GATE=0 in the environment; headless runs\n55\t(CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT != \"cli\", e.g. `claude -p`) are never held; prompts beginning with \"<\"\n56\t(task notifications and other harness-generated prompts) are never held.\n57\t\n58\tDesign rules: never raise; hooks exit 0 except the deliberate exit-2 hold; everything logged to\n59\t~/.claude/orchestration/gate.log; state under ~/.claude/orchestration/sessions/<session_id>.json.\n60\t\"\"\"\n61\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n62\t\n63\timport datetime as _dt\n64\timport json\n65\timport os\n66\timport pathlib\n67\timport re\n68\timport subprocess\n69\timport sys\n70\timport tempfile\n71\timport time\n72\t\n73\t_HARDCODED_DEFAULT_MODEL = \"claude-fable-5-1\"  # last-resort fallback if env and every settings file fail\n74\t_HARDCODED_DEFAULT_LABEL = \"Fable 5.1\"\n75\t_ALIAS_LABELS = {\"fable\": \"Fable 5.1\", \"opus\": \"Opus 5\", \"sonnet\": \"Sonnet 5\", \"haiku\": \"Haiku 4.5\"}\n76\tPROJECT_SETTINGS_NAMES = (\"settings.local.json\", \"settings.json\")  # under <cwd>/.claude/, first hit wins\n77\t\n78\t_BRACKET_SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(r\"\\[[^\\]]*\\]\\s*$\")\n79\t\n80\t\n81\tdef _settings_path() -> pathlib.Path:\n82\t    return pathlib.Path(os.environ.get(\"ORCHESTRATOR_SETTINGS_PATH\", os.path.expanduser(\"~/.claude/settings.json\")))\n83\t\n84\t\n85\tdef _strip_bracket_suffix(model_id: str) -> str:\n86\t    \"\"\"claude-fable-5-1[1m] -> claude-fable-5-1; a value with no suffix passes through unchanged.\"\"\"\n87\t    return _BRACKET_SUFFIX_RE.sub(\"\", model_id).strip()\n88\t\n89\t\n90\tdef _model_from_settings(path: pathlib.Path) -> str | None:\n91\t    \"\"\"The `model` key of a Claude Code settings file, bracket suffix stripped; None when the file\n92\t    is missing, malformed, or the key is absent or not a non-empty string (never raises).\"\"\"\n93\t    try:\n94\t        model = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")).get(\"model\")\n95\t        if isinstance(model, str) and model.strip():\n96\t            return _strip_bracket_suffix(model) or None\n97\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 -- never crash a session start over a settings-file problem\n98\t        pass\n99\t    return None\n100\t\n101\t\n102\tdef resolve_required(cwd: str | None) -> tuple[str, str]:\n103\t    \"\"\"(required model id, where it came from). Order (project-override ruling 2026-09-19, which\n104\t    supersedes lead ruling 4a of 2026-09-15: `/model` rewrites the GLOBAL settings.json as \"your\n105\t    default for new sessions\", so switching models in one project silently changed the required\n106\t    orchestrator in every other project):\n107\t    (a) env ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED_MODEL\n108\t    (b) the `model` key of <cwd>/.claude/settings.local.json, then <cwd>/.claude/settings.json\n109\t        (Claude Code reads the same key at launch, so a project pinned here both starts on and\n110\t        is gated to that model)\n111\t    (c) the `model` key of ~/.claude/settings.json (see _settings_path)\n112\t    (d) the hardcoded default\n113\t    \"\"\"\n114\t    env_val = os.environ.get(\"ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED_MODEL\", \"\")\n115\t    if env_val:\n116\t        return env_val, \"env ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED_MODEL\"\n117\t    if cwd:\n118\t        for name in PROJECT_SETTINGS_NAMES:\n119\t            p = pathlib.Path(cwd) / \".claude\" / name\n120\t            model = _model_from_settings(p)\n121\t            if model:\n122\t                return model, f\"project {p}\"\n123\t    model = _model_from_settings(_settings_path())\n124\t    if model:\n125\t        return model, f\"user {_settings_path()}\"\n126\t    return _HARDCODED_DEFAULT_MODEL, \"hardcoded default\"\n127\t\n128\t\n129\tdef _label_for(model: str) -> str:\n130\t    env_val = os.environ.get(\"ORCHESTRATOR_REQUIRED_LABEL\", \"\")\n131\t    if env_val:\n132\t        return env_val\n133\t    if model == _HARDCODED_DEFAULT_MODEL:\n134\t        return _HARDCODED_DEFAULT_LABEL\n135\t    return _ALIAS_LABELS.get(model, model)\n136\t\n137\t\n138\tREQUIRED_MODEL = \"\"  # id substring; set by configure_required()\n139\tREQUIRED_LABEL = \"\"\n140\tREQUIRED_SOURCE = \"\"\n141\tPOLICY_LINE = \"\"\n142\tGATE_PATH_SHORT = \"~/.claude/hooks/orchestrator_gate.py\"\n143\t\n144\t\n145\tdef configure_required(cwd: str | None) -> None:\n146\t    \"\"\"Rebind REQUIRED_MODEL/REQUIRED_LABEL/REQUIRED_SOURCE (and POLICY_LINE, which quotes the\n147\t    label) for the project at `cwd`. Called at the top of every subcommand that has a payload or\n148\t    session state; a falsy `cwd` resolves against the process cwd, which for hooks is the\n149\t    project directory anyway.\"\"\"\n150\t    global REQUIRED_MODEL, REQUIRED_LABEL, REQUIRED_SOURCE, POLICY_LINE\n151\t    REQUIRED_MODEL, REQUIRED_SOURCE = resolve_required(cwd or os.getcwd())\n152\t    REQUIRED_LABEL = _label_for(REQUIRED_MODEL)\n153\t    POLICY_LINE = _build_policy_line(REQUIRED_LABEL)\n154\t\n155\t\n156\tdef gate_enabled() -> bool:  # read live so CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_GATE=0 works per process and in self-test\n157\t    return os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_GATE\", \"1\") != \"0\"\n158\t\n159\t\n160\tSTATE_ROOT = pathlib.Path(os.environ.get(\"ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_DIR\", os.path.expanduser(\"~/.claude/orchestration\")))\n161\tHOOKS_DIR = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent\n162\tINNER_STATUSLINE = HOOKS_DIR / \"statusline_inner.sh\"\n163\tSESSION_TTL_DAYS = 30\n164\tHELD_PROMPT_KEEP_CHARS = 4000\n165\t\n166\tCONFIRM_PHRASE_RE = re.compile(r\"confirm\\s+orchestrator|orchestrator[:\\s]+confirm\", re.IGNORECASE)\n167\tSTATUS_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*orchestrator[:\\s]+status\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\n168\t# Menu answers, valid only while the gate is armed for the session (see classify_answer).\n169\tANSWER_KEEP_RE = re.compile(r\"^(?:option\\s*)?(?:2\\b|keep\\b|yes\\b|y\\b|ok(?:ay)?\\b|confirm\\b)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n170\tANSWER_SWITCH_RE = re.compile(r\"^(?:option\\s*)?(?:1\\b|switch\\b)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n171\tANSWER_RESTART_RE = re.compile(r\"^(?:option\\s*)?(?:3\\b|restart\\b|stop\\b|exit\\b|quit\\b)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n172\t\n173\tdef _build_policy_line(required_label: str) -> str:\n174\t    return (\n175\t        f\"ORCHESTRATION HIERARCHY (global, {GATE_PATH_SHORT}): this session is the supervisory \"\n176\t        f\"orchestrator and is expected to run on {required_label}; it keeps decomposition, synthesis, \"\n177\t        \"critique and decisions, and delegates everything else to cheaper subagents: scout-haiku \"\n178\t        \"(read-only lookups, big-file reads, greps), clerk-haiku (mechanical state changes: git \"\n179\t        \"add/commit/push on the user's word, running named commands, bulk or large-file edits), \"\n180\t        \"worker-sonnet (default builder; CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL), worker-opus (hard, judgment-heavy \"\n181\t        \"but bounded subtasks); isolation: worktree when they mutate tracked files in parallel; normal \"\n182\t        \"parallel cap 3, burst 6. Do inline only what costs less than a dispatch: one short command, a \"\n183\t        \"read under ~200 lines, a one-line edit. `fork` inherits the orchestrator model: use it only when \"\n184\t        \"the subtask needs this full context.\"\n185\t    )\n186\t\n187\t\n188\tconfigure_required(None)\n189\t\n190\t\n191\t# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers\n192\tdef now_iso() -> str:\n193\t    return _dt.datetime.now().astimezone().replace(microsecond=0).isoformat()\n194\t\n195\t\n196\tdef log(msg: str) -> None:\n197\t    try:\n198\t        STATE_ROOT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n199\t        with (STATE_ROOT / \"gate.log\").open(\"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n200\t            fh.write(f\"{now_iso()} {msg}\\n\")\n201\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n202\t        pass\n203\t\n204\t\n205\tdef read_stdin_json() -> tuple[dict, str]:\n206\t    try:\n207\t        raw = sys.stdin.read()\n208\t        return (json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}), raw\n209\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n210\t        return {}, \"\"\n211\t\n212\t\n213\tdef session_file(session_id: str) -> pathlib.Path:\n214\t    safe = re.sub(r\"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]\", \"_\", session_id or \"unknown\")\n215\t    return STATE_ROOT / \"sessions\" / f\"{safe}.json\"\n216\t\n217\t\n218\tdef load_state(session_id: str) -> dict:\n219\t    try:\n220\t        return json.loads(session_file(session_id).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n221\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n222\t        return {}\n223\t\n224\t\n225\tdef save_state(session_id: str, state: dict) -> None:\n226\t    try:\n227\t        p = session_file(session_id)\n228\t        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n229\t        state[\"session_id\"] = session_id\n230\t        state[\"updated_at\"] = now_iso()\n231\t        tmp = p.with_suffix(\".tmp\")\n232\t        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n233\t        os.replace(tmp, p)\n234\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n235\t        pass\n236\t\n237\t\n238\tdef prune_old_sessions() -> None:\n239\t    try:\n240\t        cutoff = time.time() - SESSION_TTL_DAYS * 86400\n241\t        for p in (STATE_ROOT / \"sessions\").glob(\"*.json\"):\n242\t            if p.stat().st_mtime < cutoff:\n243\t                p.unlink()\n244\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n245\t        pass\n246\t\n247\t\n248\tdef is_required(model_id: str | None) -> bool:\n249\t    return bool(model_id) and REQUIRED_MODEL in model_id\n250\t\n251\t\n252\tdef entrypoint() -> str:\n253\t    return os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT\", \"\") or \"unknown\"\n254\t\n255\t\n256\tdef interactive() -> bool:\n257\t    return entrypoint() == \"cli\"\n258\t\n259\t\n260\tdef is_confirmed(state: dict, model_id: str | None) -> bool:\n261\t    return bool(state.get(\"confirmed\")) and state.get(\"confirmed_model\") == model_id\n262\t\n263\t\n264\tCONTEXT_NUDGE_MIN = 50   # first band that earns a handoff nudge\n265\tCONTEXT_HARD_CEILING = 60  # band at which the wording becomes \"take no new work\"\n266\t\n267\t\n268\tdef context_pct(payload: dict) -> int | None:\n269\t    \"\"\"context_window.used_percentage from a statusLine payload, as an int; None if absent/invalid.\"\"\"\n270\t    cw = payload.get(\"context_window\")\n271\t    if not isinstance(cw, dict):\n272\t        return None\n273\t    try:\n274\t        v = cw.get(\"used_percentage\")\n275\t        return int(float(v)) if v is not None and not isinstance(v, bool) else None\n276\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n277\t        return None\n278\t\n279\t\n280\tBOUNDARY_GIT_TIMEOUT = 0.3          # seconds per git call; a slow repo is skipped, never blocking\n281\tBOUNDARY_IGNORE_PREFIXES = (\".claude/handoffs/auto/\", \"logs/\")\n282\tBOUNDARY_IGNORE_SUFFIXES = (\".DS_Store\",)\n283\tBOUNDARY_BRANCH_GLOB = \"refs/heads/agent/\"\n284\tHANDOFF_LATEST = \"docs/handoffs/LATEST.md\"\n285\tHANDOFF_HEAD_RE = re.compile(r\"HEAD\\D{0,12}?\\b([0-9a-fA-F]{7,40})\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\n286\tNUDGE_MAX_CHARS = 300\n287\t\n288\t\n289\tdef _git(cwd: str, *args: str) -> str:\n290\t    \"\"\"One git call, short-leashed. Raises on failure/timeout; callers turn that into `skipped`.\"\"\"\n291\t    out = subprocess.run(\n292\t        [\"git\", *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=BOUNDARY_GIT_TIMEOUT\n293\t    )\n294\t    if out.returncode != 0:\n295\t        raise RuntimeError(f\"git {args[0]} rc={out.returncode}\")\n296\t    return out.stdout\n297\t\n298\t\n299\tdef _porcelain_path(line: str) -> str:\n300\t    \"\"\"Path part of a `git status --porcelain` line, taking the destination of a rename.\"\"\"\n301\t    path = line[3:] if len(line) > 3 else \"\"\n302\t    if \" -> \" in path:\n303\t        path = path.split(\" -> \", 1)[1]\n304\t    return path.strip().strip('\"')\n305\t\n306\t\n307\tdef _boundary_ignored(path: str) -> bool:\n308\t    return path.startswith(BOUNDARY_IGNORE_PREFIXES) or path.endswith(BOUNDARY_IGNORE_SUFFIXES)\n309\t\n310\t\n311\tdef _handoff_commits(cwd: str) -> int | None:\n312\t    \"\"\"Commits on HEAD since the sha named by docs/handoffs/LATEST.md; None when not determinable.\"\"\"\n313\t    latest = pathlib.Path(cwd) / HANDOFF_LATEST\n314\t    if not latest.is_file():\n315\t        return None\n316\t    try:\n317\t        text = latest.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n318\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n319\t        return None\n320\t    sha = None\n321\t    for ln in text.splitlines():\n322\t        m = HANDOFF_HEAD_RE.search(ln)\n323\t        if m:\n324\t            sha = m.group(1)\n325\t            break\n326\t    if not sha:\n327\t        return None\n328\t    try:\n329\t        return int(_git(cwd, \"rev-list\", \"--count\", f\"{sha}..HEAD\").strip())\n330\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n331\t        return None  # sha unknown to this repo, or git unhappy: context only, never a blocker\n332\t\n333\t\n334\tdef boundary_state(cwd: str) -> dict | None:\n335\t    \"\"\"Advisory read-only verdict on whether `cwd`'s repo is at a clean task boundary.\n336\t\n337\t    None when cwd is not inside a git work tree. Otherwise\n338\t    {\"at_boundary\": bool, \"reasons\": [str], \"commits_since_handoff\": int|None, \"skipped\": str|None}.\n339\t    Every git call is capped at BOUNDARY_GIT_TIMEOUT; on timeout or any error the verdict degrades\n340\t    to at_boundary=False with `skipped` set. Never raises, never writes, never blocks a prompt.\n341\t    \"\"\"\n342\t    if not cwd or not os.path.isdir(cwd):\n343\t        return None\n344\t    try:\n345\t        if _git(cwd, \"rev-parse\", \"--is-inside-work-tree\").strip() != \"true\":\n346\t            return None\n347\t    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n348\t        return {\"at_boundary\": False, \"reasons\": [], \"commits_since_handoff\": None, \"skipped\": \"git slow\"}\n349\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n350\t        return None  # not a repo (or no git at all): nothing to say\n351\t\n352\t    reasons: list[str] = []\n353\t    try:\n354\t        # `--untracked-files=normal` collapses an untracked directory to \"dir/\", which would hide\n355\t        # whether everything under it is ignorable (.claude/handoffs/auto/, logs/, *.DS_Store).\n356\t        # Those collapsed entries are re-listed with -uall, scoped to the directory, so the ignore\n357\t        # rule always sees real file paths; tracked changes still come from the normal run.\n358\t        dirty: list[str] = []\n359\t        collapsed: list[str] = []\n360\t        for ln in _git(cwd, \"status\", \"--porcelain\", \"--untracked-files=normal\").splitlines():\n361\t            if not ln.strip():\n362\t                continue\n363\t            path = _porcelain_path(ln)\n364\t            if ln.startswith(\"??\") and path.endswith(\"/\"):\n365\t                collapsed.append(path)\n366\t            elif not _boundary_ignored(path):\n367\t                dirty.append(path)\n368\t        for d in collapsed:\n369\t            try:\n370\t                expanded = [\n371\t                    _porcelain_path(x) for x in\n372\t                    _git(cwd, \"status\", \"--porcelain\", \"--untracked-files=all\", \"--\", d).splitlines()\n373\t                    if x.strip()\n374\t                ]\n375\t            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n376\t                raise\n377\t            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n378\t                expanded = [d]\n379\t            dirty.extend(p for p in expanded if not _boundary_ignored(p))\n380\t        if dirty:\n381\t            reasons.append(f\"uncommitted edits in {len(dirty)} file{'s' if len(dirty) != 1 else ''}\")\n382\t\n383\t        main = \"main\"\n384\t        try:\n385\t            _git(cwd, \"rev-parse\", \"--verify\", \"--quiet\", \"refs/heads/main\")\n386\t        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n387\t            main = \"master\"\n388\t        branches = [b for b in _git(cwd, \"for-each-ref\", \"--format=%(refname:short)\",\n389\t                                    BOUNDARY_BRANCH_GLOB).splitlines() if b.strip()]\n390\t        unmerged: list[str] = []\n391\t        for br in branches:\n392\t            try:\n393\t                n = int(_git(cwd, \"rev-list\", \"--count\", f\"{main}..{br}\").strip())\n394\t            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n395\t                raise\n396\t            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n397\t                continue\n398\t            if n > 0:\n399\t                unmerged.append(f\"{n} unmerged commit{'s' if n != 1 else ''} on {br}\")\n400\t        if unmerged:\n401\t            shown = \"; \".join(unmerged[:2])\n402\t            if len(unmerged) > 2:\n403\t                shown += f\"; +{len(unmerged) - 2} more\"\n404\t            reasons.append(shown)\n405\t\n406\t        commits = _handoff_commits(cwd)\n407\t    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n408\t        return {\"at_boundary\": False, \"reasons\": [], \"commits_since_handoff\": None, \"skipped\": \"git slow\"}\n409\t    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001\n410\t        return {\"at_boundary\": False, \"reasons\": [], \"commits_since_handoff\": None,\n411\t                \"skipped\": type(exc).__name__.lower()[:20] or \"git error\"}\n412\t\n413\t    return {\"at_boundary\": not reasons, \"reasons\": reasons, \"commits_since_handoff\": commits, \"skipped\": None}\n414\t\n415\t\n416\tdef _boundary_clause(b: dict) -> str:\n417\t    \"\"\"The verdict fragment appended inside the nudge brackets.\"\"\"\n418\t    if b[\"at_boundary\"]:\n419\t        k = b.get(\"commits_since_handoff\")\n420\t        return \"boundary reached\" + (f\" ({k} commits since last handoff)\" if k is not None else \"\")\n421\t    if b[\"reasons\"]:\n422\t        return \"not at a boundary: \" + \"; \".join(b[\"reasons\"])\n423\t    return \"not at a boundary\"\n424\t\n425\t\n426\tdef context_nudge(sid: str, state: dict, cwd: str | None = None) -> str:\n427\t    \"\"\"One line when the session enters a new 10-point context band at or above CONTEXT_NUDGE_MIN,\n428\t    or when the repo's task-boundary verdict has flipped since the last line we emitted.\"\"\"\n429\t    try:\n430\t        pct = int(state.get(\"context_pct\"))\n431\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n432\t        return \"\"\n433\t    if pct < CONTEXT_NUDGE_MIN:\n434\t        return \"\"\n435\t    band = pct // 10\n436\t    band_new = int(state.get(\"context_nudge_band\", -1)) < band\n437\t\n438\t    b = boundary_state(cwd or state.get(\"cwd\") or os.getcwd())\n439\t    verdict = None if b is None else bool(b[\"at_boundary\"])\n440\t    prev = state.get(\"context_boundary_last\", \"unset\")\n441\t    if not band_new and (prev != \"unset\" and prev == verdict):\n442\t        return \"\"\n443\t\n444\t    state[\"context_nudge_band\"] = max(band, int(state.get(\"context_nudge_band\", -1)))\n445\t    state[\"context_boundary_last\"] = verdict\n446\t    save_state(sid, state)\n447\t\n448\t    tail = \"finish the current verification, then /handoff <slug> and /clear\"\n449\t    if b is None:  # outside a git repo: today's wording, unchanged\n450\t        if pct >= CONTEXT_HARD_CEILING:\n451\t            return f\"[context {pct}% — hard ceiling: take no new work in this session; {tail}]\"\n452\t        return f\"[context {pct}% — handoff zone: {tail}]\"\n453\t\n454\t    clause = _boundary_clause(b)\n455\t    skipped = f\"; boundary check skipped ({b['skipped']})\" if b.get(\"skipped\") else \"\"\n456\t    if pct >= CONTEXT_HARD_CEILING:\n457\t        line = f\"[context {pct}% — hard ceiling: take no new work in this session; {tail}; {clause}{skipped}]\"\n458\t    elif b[\"at_boundary\"]:\n459\t        line = f\"[context {pct}% — handoff zone: {clause}; /handoff <slug> and /clear now{skipped}]\"\n460\t    else:\n461\t        line = f\"[context {pct}% — handoff zone: {clause}; {tail}{skipped}]\"\n462\t    line = line.replace(\"\\n\", \" \")\n463\t    if len(line) > NUDGE_MAX_CHARS:\n464\t        line = line[: NUDGE_MAX_CHARS - 2].rstrip() + \"…]\"\n465\t    return line\n466\t\n467\t\n468\tdef record_model(payload: dict) -> dict | None:\n469\t    \"\"\"Record model.id from a statusLine-shaped payload. Returns the state written, or None.\"\"\"\n470\t    sid = payload.get(\"session_id\") or \"\"\n471\t    model = payload.get(\"model\") or {}\n472\t    model_id = model.get(\"id\") if isinstance(model, dict) else None\n473\t    if not sid or not model_id:\n474\t        return None\n475\t    state = load_state(sid)\n476\t    prev = state.get(\"model_id\")\n477\t    state[\"model_id\"] = model_id\n478\t    state[\"model_display\"] = model.get(\"display_name\") or model_id\n479\t    state[\"model_source\"] = \"statusline\"\n480\t    state.setdefault(\"cwd\", payload.get(\"cwd\") or (payload.get(\"workspace\") or {}).get(\"current_dir\"))\n481\t    pct = context_pct(payload)\n482\t    if pct is not None:\n483\t        state[\"context_pct\"] = pct\n484\t    if prev and prev != model_id and state.get(\"confirmed_model\") not in (None, model_id):\n485\t        state[\"confirmed\"] = False  # a /model switch after confirming re-arms the gate\n486\t    save_state(sid, state)\n487\t    if prev != model_id:\n488\t        log(f\"record sid={sid[:8]} model={model_id} (was {prev})\")\n489\t    return state\n490\t\n491\t\n492\tdef model_from_transcript(path: str | None) -> str | None:\n493\t    \"\"\"Last assistant entry's message.model, scanning only the tail of the transcript.\"\"\"\n494\t    if not path:\n495\t        return None\n496\t    try:\n497\t        p = pathlib.Path(path)\n498\t        size = p.stat().st_size\n499\t        with p.open(\"rb\") as fh:\n500\t            fh.seek(max(0, size - 400_000))\n501\t            tail = fh.read().decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n502\t        found = None\n503\t        for ln in tail.splitlines():\n504\t            if '\"assistant\"' not in ln or '\"model\"' not in ln:\n505\t                continue\n506\t            try:\n507\t                d = json.loads(ln)\n508\t            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n509\t                continue\n510\t            if d.get(\"type\") == \"assistant\":\n511\t                m = (d.get(\"message\") or {}).get(\"model\")\n512\t                if m:\n513\t                    found = m\n514\t        return found\n515\t    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n516\t        return None\n517\t\n518\t\n519\tdef detect_model(payload: dict) -> tuple[str | None, str]:\n520\t    \"\"\"(model_id or None, source) using the recorded statusline value first, then the transcript.\"\"\"\n521\t    sid = payload.get(\"session_id\") or \"\"\n522\t    state = load_state(sid)\n523\t    if state.get(\"model_id\"):\n524\t        return state[\"model_id\"], state.get(\"model_source\") or \"statusline\"\n525\t    m = model_from_transcript(payload.get(\"transcript_path\"))\n526\t    if m:\n527\t        state[\"model_id\"] = m\n528\t        state[\"model_source\"] = \"transcript\"\n529\t        save_state(sid, state)\n530\t        return m, \"transcript\"\n531\t    return None, \"unknown\"\n532\t\n533\t\n534\t# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- messages\n535\tdef confirm_cmd(sid: str, model_id: str | None) -> str:\n536\t    cmd = f\"python3 {GATE_PATH_SHORT} confirm --session {sid}\"\n537\t    return cmd if model_id else cmd + \" --model <your model id>\"\n538\t\n539\t\n540\tdef menu_directive(sid: str, model_id: str | None) -> str:\n541\t    \"\"\"Injected context telling Claude to run the AskUserQuestion menu before acting.\"\"\"\n542\t    who = f\"runs on {model_id}\" if model_id else \"has an unrecorded model\"\n543\t    lead = (\n544\t        f\"[orchestrator gate] ACTIVE: this session {who}, not (confirmed as) {REQUIRED_LABEL} \"\n545\t        f\"({REQUIRED_MODEL}). State the model id you are running as.\"\n546\t        if model_id is None\n547\t        else f\"[orchestrator gate] ACTIVE: this session {who}, not {REQUIRED_LABEL} ({REQUIRED_MODEL}).\"\n548\t    )\n549\t    return (\n550\t        f\"{lead} Do NOT act on the prompt yet. First call AskUserQuestion with exactly these three \"\n551\t        \"options, in this order: \"\n552\t        f\"(1) Switch to {REQUIRED_LABEL}: reply that the hook cannot switch models, tell the user to type \"\n553\t        f\"/model {REQUIRED_MODEL} and re-send the prompt, then stop. \"\n554\t        f\"(2) Keep {model_id or 'this model'} for this session: run `{confirm_cmd(sid, model_id)}` via Bash, \"\n555\t        \"then carry out the prompt. \"\n556\t        \"(3) Stop: do nothing. \"\n557\t        \"Until confirmed, the hook holds every later ordinary prompt; there the user may answer with \"\n558\t        \"1/2/3, `keep`, or `confirm orchestrator`.\"\n559\t    )\n560\t\n561\t\n562\tdef hold_message(sid: str, model_id: str) -> str:\n563\t    return (\n564\t        f\"[orchestrator gate] HELD: this session's model is {model_id}, not {REQUIRED_LABEL} \"\n565\t        f\"({REQUIRED_MODEL}), and it is not yet confirmed as the supervisory orchestrator. Your prompt \"\n566\t        \"was not sent; it is remembered and will be handed to Claude once you answer. Reply with one of:\\n\"\n567\t        f\"  1  switch: type the slash command   /model {REQUIRED_MODEL}   then re-send your prompt\\n\"\n568\t        f\"  2  keep {model_id} for this session   (also accepted: keep, yes, confirm orchestrator)\\n\"\n569\t        f\"  3  restart: /exit, then   claude --model {REQUIRED_MODEL} --resume {sid}\\n\"\n570\t        \"Headless runs (claude -p) and CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_GATE=0 bypass this gate. \"\n571\t        f\"State: python3 {GATE_PATH_SHORT} status\"\n572\t    )\n573\t\n574\t\n575\tdef switch_message(model_id: str) -> str:\n576\t    return (\n577\t        f\"[orchestrator gate] The hook cannot switch models. Type the slash command   /model {REQUIRED_MODEL}   \"\n578\t        \"now (Claude Code handles it locally; it is not sent to the model), then re-send your prompt. \"\n579\t        f\"To keep {model_id} instead, reply 2.\"\n580\t    )\n581\t\n582\t\n583\tdef restart_message(sid: str, model_id: str) -> str:\n584\t    return (\n585\t        f\"[orchestrator gate] To restart on {REQUIRED_LABEL}: type /exit, then run   \"\n586\t        f\"claude --model {REQUIRED_MODEL} --resume {sid}   (drop --resume for a fresh session). \"\n587\t        f\"To keep {model_id} instead, reply 2.\"\n588\t    )\n589\t\n590\t\n591\tdef classify_answer(prompt: str) -> str | None:\n592\t    \"\"\"'keep' | 'switch' | 'restart' | None for a prompt sent while the gate is armed.\"\"\"\n593\t    text = prompt.strip()\n594\t    if CONFIRM_PHRASE_RE.search(text):\n595\t        return \"keep\"\n596\t    if ANSWER_KEEP_RE.match(text):\n597\t        return \"keep\"\n598\t    if ANSWER_SWITCH_RE.match(text):\n599\t        return \"switch\"\n600\t    if ANSWER_RESTART_RE.match(text):\n601\t        return \"restart\"\n602\t    return None\n603\t\n604\t\n605\tdef do_confirm(sid: str, state: dict, model_id: str, how: str) -> str:\n606\t    state[\"confirmed\"] = True\n607\t    state[\"confirmed_model\"] = model_id\n608\t    state[\"confirmed_at\"] = now_iso()\n609\t    state[\"confirmed_via\"] = how\n610\t    held_prompt = state.pop(\"held_prompt\", None)\n611\t    save_state(sid, state)\n612\t    log(f\"confirm sid={sid[:8]} model={model_id} via={how}\")\n613\t    msg = (\n614\t        f\"[orchestrator gate] The user confirmed {model_id} as the supervisory orchestrator for this \"\n615\t        \"session. Acknowledge in one line; the delegation policy still applies to subagents.\"\n616\t    )\n617\t    if held_prompt:\n618\t        msg += f\" The prompt that was held is below; carry it out now:\\n{held_prompt}\"\n619\t    return msg\n620\t\n621\t\n622\t# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- routing\n623\t# Cheap-task routing: a rule table, not a model. It only injects a hint; the orchestrator decides.\n624\t_JUDGMENT_RE = re.compile(\n625\t    r\"\\b(?:why|fix|debug|diagnos\\w*|design|decide|should|explain|review|critique|plan|refactor|\"\n626\t    r\"implement|architect\\w*|investigat\\w*|figure out|think|compare|evaluate|assess)\\b\",\n627\t    re.IGNORECASE,\n628\t)\n629\t_CLERK_RULES = [\n630\t    (re.compile(r\"^(?:please\\s+|now\\s+|go ahead and\\s+|just\\s+)?(?:git\\s+)?(?:push|commit|stage|stash|tag|amend)\\b\", re.I), \"git operation\"),\n631\t    (re.compile(r\"\\bgit\\s+(?:add|commit|push|stash|tag|mv|rm)\\b\", re.I), \"git operation\"),\n632\t    (re.compile(r\"^(?:please\\s+|now\\s+|just\\s+)?(?:re)?run\\b\", re.I), \"run a named command\"),\n633\t    (re.compile(r\"^(?:please\\s+)?(?:rename|mv|delete|remove|rm|move|copy|cp|chmod|touch|mkdir)\\b\", re.I), \"file operation\"),\n634\t    (re.compile(r\"\\b(?:find|search)\\s+and\\s+replace\\b|\\breplace\\s+all\\b|\\bsed\\s+-i\\b|\\bbulk\\s+(?:edit|rename|replace)\\b\", re.I), \"bulk edit\"),\n635\t
